title: Fresh Faces in Durham: Breaking Down the 8 Newcomers Driving UNH Basketball’s Early-Season Push - NGSC Sports
content:
DURHAM, N.H. — Off to a 2-1 start, the University of New Hampshire Wildcats men’s basketball team is looking to make serious waves in the America East Conference. Head coach Nathan Davis has re-tooled his squad by welcoming eight new players to Durham, building the depth, size, and perimeter firepower needed for a conference title run. Here is an in-depth look at the eight newcomers making up UNH’s revamped roster. Ryan Zan and Josiah Coleman both scored 15 points in Thursday night’s victory at Rider. 🎟️ https://t.co/v1mFPumBC8 After spending last season at Fairfield, Zan has hit the ground running in Durham. The 6-foot-7 forward has logged 93 total minutes across three games, averaging 12.3 points per contest. Zan is shooting 41.9% from the field (13-of-31), 33.3% from three-point territory (5-of-15), and 75.0% from the free-throw line (6-of-8), giving the Wildcats an immediate scoring engine in the frontcourt. Arriving by way of Weatherford College, Coleman has stepped right into a major backcourt role. Through three games, the 6-foot-4 guard is averaging 9.0 points per game in 90 total minutes. He has proven adept at getting to the line, shooting 82.4% on free throws (14-of-17) alongside a 42.9% field-goal percentage (6-of-14). A transfer from Manhattan College—where he logged 26 appearances (19 starts), shot 44.3% (31-of-70), and blocked 23 shots—Oliver-Bush brings length and perimeter defense to the lineup. The 6-foot-5 guard has logged 78 minutes across UNH’s first three games, averaging 8.7 points per game while connecting on 2-of-7 (28.6%) attempts from beyond the arc. McKenna joins UNH following a season at Old Dominion where he averaged 4.0 points on 41.7% shooting with 66 rebounds and 14 steals in 26 games. Through 57 total minutes in Durham, he is averaging 4.7 points per game and has grabbed 16 defensive rebounds. Squire comes to Durham after starting all 30 games for River State College last season, where he averaged 14.3 points on 38.9% shooting. A perimeter threat and playmaker, he drained 72 three-pointers (35.5%), hit 80.0% of his free throws, and totaled 120 assists and 118 rebounds. Squire is currently working into the rotation as he awaits his official UNH debut. A 6-foot-5 freshman guard hailing from Oakland, California, by way of Overtime Elite in Atlanta, Georgia, Faumuina has logged three minutes of action across the first three games as he adjusts to the college game. A local 6-foot-5 freshman guard from Salem, New Hampshire, who prepped at Loomis Chaffee, Sangermano adds depth to the Wildcats’ backcourt as he competes for his first regular-season collegiate minutes. The 6-foot-8 transfer forward arrives from St. Thomas University. Myers has logged 10 total minutes in three games, pulling down one rebound as he competes for frontcourt rotation snaps. With a balanced mix of proven Division I transfers, dynamic junior college scorers, and high-upside freshmen, Coach Davis has built a roster with the versatility to make noise in the America East this season. title: UNH Manchester Earns Top Regional College Rankings from U.S. News & World Report - University of New Hampshire
content: The University of New Hampshire at Manchester has been named a top regional college in the north by U.S. News & World Report in its 2027 Best Colleges rankings. UNH Manchester ranked No. 8 overall among Regional Colleges in the North and, within that category, ranked No. 3 in Top Public Schools and No. 2 for Social Mobility, recognizing the university's academic quality, accessibility, and commitment to student success. The No. 2 ranking for social mobility is particularly significant, highlighting UNH Manchester's success in enrolling and graduating students who receive federal Pell Grants, which are typically awarded to undergraduate students with significant financial need. "There's no single path to earning a college degree, and we see that reflected in the students who come to UNH Manchester," says Dawn Albertson, interim dean of UNH Manchester. "Our goal is to give every student the support, experiences, and opportunities to succeed, and it's especially meaningful to see that commitment recognized." Through merit scholarships, need-based financial aid, and personalized support services, UNH Manchester works to make a UNH education possible for students and families. Nearly half (45%) of UNH Manchester students graduate with zero debt, underscoring the university's commitment to making higher education accessible and affordable. Small class sizes, individualized advising, and close faculty relationships create a supportive learning environment where students can thrive academically and professionally. Located in Manchester's historic Millyard, the campus also connects students with the industries driving New Hampshire's economy. According to the First Destination Survey of 2025 graduates, 64% of students participated in at least one internship during their time at UNH Manchester. This focus on internships as well as research and hands-on learning allows students to gain professional experience, build industry connections, and prepare for careers in their chosen fields. Within six months of graduation, 91% were employed or continuing their education, with 88% of those employed working in a field related to their major. Together, the rankings underscore UNH Manchester's distinctive approach to higher education: combining the academic quality of a UNH degree with the affordability, individual attention, and career-focused opportunities of a small, city campus. title: UNH Celebrates Outstanding Educators with 2026 Faculty Excellence Awards - University of New Hampshire
content: Every year, a chosen few of UNH’s outstanding faculty members from each college and school receive Faculty Excellence Awards in recognition of their achievements in teaching, scholarship and service. University-wide awards recognize public service, research, teaching and engagement. The 2026 award recipients include: Mike Alvarez, 2026 Outstanding Assistant Professor Award, COLA ProfessorAlvarez is an exemplary teacher and scholar whose uniquely personal approach to the study of communication has expanded the breadth and depth of understanding for students and colleagues alike. He has literally set new records for the number of awards and presentations that a single scholar has received or given at a single national conference. He is a powerhouse of productivity, with multiple book projects underway at any given time. One of his earliest manuscripts, “Unraveling: An Autoethnography of Suicide and Renewal,” received a Book Award from an international panel of reviewers. He shows no signs of slowing down and pulls no punches in his study of even the most difficult topics. His work is powerful enough to break through the noise and reach high-profile platforms like the New York Times and The Filipino Express. Cristy Beemer, 2026 Graduate Faculty Mentor Award, COLA Professor Beemer — an unusual scholar in that she has several seemingly divergent areas of expertise, from Shakespeare to composition — has been a consistent and tireless mentor for graduate students in the English department since she arrived on campus in 2008. She develops rapport with students and builds on that rapport to motivate them not only to work toward excellence, but also to develop standards of excellence that match their unique aspirations. Professor Beemer arranges mock interviews for composition graduate students who are preparing to enter the job market. They are united in expressing their gratitude for this opportunity to practice fielding questions, sometimes giving a lecture to faculty and peers, and then receiving valuable feedback. She has chaired more than a dozen dissertations and served on many more exam and dissertation committees. Professor Beemer’s mentees earn prestigious awards in their disciplines, and 100% are successful in the job market. Student evaluations reflect their gratitude for Professor Beemer’s contributions to their success — these evaluations approach the spectacular. Mentorship doesn’t get better than this. The English Department is honored to have her step into the role of graduate director for the next three years. Scott Berube, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, Paul College Since joining UNH in 2004, Scott Berube has challenged and supported countless undergraduate and graduate students, earning a reputation for making accounting's most demanding concepts feel engaging, relevant and — dare we say it — fun. Even with hundreds of students each semester, he makes every one of them feel seen. He reaches out after exams to celebrate strong work,  and is always there when someone needs help. Add his famous "Berube Bucks," instructional videos, and real-world cases from his years as a CPA and fraud examiner, and students leave his classes more confident and resilient. Former student Landis Nadeau puts it best: "You will always have someone in your corner at UNH who wants you to win and is always prepared to help you do it." As director of the Master's in Accounting program, Scott helped launch the Financial Leadership pathway. His trust-fall video promoting the pathway became one of Paul College's most-viewed, and enrollment has more than doubled on his watch. Through his commitment to opening doors, Scott's impact reaches far beyond the classroom. Alyson Eberhardt, 2026 Excellence in Public Service Award, Extension Alyson Eberhardt exemplifies the best of public service at the University of New Hampshire. As an associate Extension professor and state specialist in coastal ecosystems, Alyson brings together science and community action to protect and strengthen New Hampshire’s seacoast. Through programs such as the Coastal Research Volunteers, the Volunteer Beach Profiling Program, and community-based dune restoration, she engages volunteers in collecting critical data and taking action to address erosion, storm impacts, habitat change, and coastal resilience. What distinguishes Alyson’s work is her combination of scientific rigor, enduring community partnerships, and genuine commitment to helping people make informed choices. Her work embodies UNH’s Land- and Sea-Grant mission and demonstrates the extraordinary value of putting knowledge into service. We are proud to recognize Alyson Eberhardt with the 2026 Excellence in Public Service Award. Jessica Ernakovich, 2026 Outstanding Associate Professor Award, COLSA Jessica Ernakovich is a professor in the Department of Natural Resources and the Environment whose research has transformed our understanding of how Arctic ecosystems respond to environmental change. Through pioneering research linking microbial communities, nutrient cycling, and ecosystem resilience, she has revealed how some of Earth’s smallest organisms shape some of its largest climate processes. In less than a decade at UNH, Jessica has built an internationally recognized research program, authored more than 40 peer-reviewed publications, and secured more than $8 million in competitive research funding, including a National Science Foundation CAREER award. Jessica’s impact extends far beyond her research. She has advised more than a dozen graduate students, mentored more than 30 undergraduate researchers, and helped her students earn prestigious awards and fellowships. Through her scientific leadership, dedication to students, and commitment to understanding a rapidly changing world, she has fundamentally changed both her field and the lives of those she mentors. Francois Foucart, 2026 Excellence in Research Award, CEPS Francois Foucart’s groundbreaking research draws upon computer simulations and theoretical physics to study collisions between black holes and neutron stars. In 2015, this topic leapt to the forefront of astrophysical research with the first-ever detection of gravitational waves from the merger of two black holes. Leading scientists across the globe attest to the quality and originality of Professor Foucart’s research and to his status as a world leader in this area. Professor Foucart has provided research mentoring to numerous undergraduates, graduate students, and postdocs and has twice secured external funding to purchase supercomputers that support research across the university. UNH is proud to honor Professor Foucart for his truly outstanding contributions. Ryan Gibson, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, COLA Ryan Gibson joined the Sociology Department as a Postdoctoral Diversity and Innovation Scholar in 2020 and was subsequently hired as a tenure track assistant professor in 2022. He quickly established himself as a star teacher as well as an exceptional colleague energetically committed to the success of UNH. Whether teaching sociological theory or courses on race and ethnicity, students “found his passion for the subject matter infectious, his ability to teach complicated material brilliant, and his skills in expanding student’s knowledge and critical thinking inspiring.” In the words of another colleague: “Ryan stood out as energetic yet grounded, enthusiastic yet centered, and deeply committed to all aspects of his role as a teacher, scholar, and colleague … he was not only someone I valued as a colleague, but someone from whom I would continually learn and often be in awe because of his [transformational] teaching, mentoring, and support of our students.” Fei Han is a scholar in infrastructure systems, geotechnical engineering, and data-driven methods whose passion for his profession is unmistakably woven into every aspect of his teaching. He has established himself as a consistently high-impact instructor whose courses are defined by energy, structure, and clarity. Students describe him as highly engaging and exceptionally clear, with a remarkable ability to make technically demanding material accessible without sacrificing rigor. His students say it best: "Han has been an incredible professor making sure that the class understands concepts in a fun and exciting way," says one student. Another student noted that he "connected with every single student and always went above and beyond." A defining strength of Han's teaching is its seamless integration with his active research program, exposing students to contemporary tools and real-world challenges in ways that are both inspiring and professionally formative. Beyond the classroom, he demonstrates a sustained commitment to mentorship, supervising doctoral students, mentoring undergraduate researchers, and contributing generously to his department and profession. Eleanor Harrison-Buck, 2026 Excellence in International Engagement Award, COLA For more than two decades, Eleanor Harrison-Buck, or Ellie, as her colleagues know her, has cultivated a research, teaching, and community partnership portfolio in Belize that is remarkable not only for its longevity, but for its depth, integrity, and positive impact on both UNH and Belizean communities. Ellie, a professor of anthropology at UNH, has directed the Belize River East Archaeology Project since 2011, earning international recognition as a leading Mayan archaeologist. She has led 13 study abroad programs, bringing more than 100 UNH students to Belize – many traveling internationally for the first time. Beyond her research and teaching, Ellie played a foundational role in establishing the Crooked Tree Museum and Cultural Heritage Center, a community-led space dedicated to preserving Belizean Kriol heritage. Her commitment to Belize is not fleeting  – it is sustained, reciprocal, and deeply rooted in partnership with the communities whose histories she studies. As someone who has modeled ethical international engagement for years, Harrison-Buck is a most deserving recipient of this recognition, and we are honored to celebrate her as the recipient of the Excellence in International Engagement Award. Douglas Lanier, 2026 Jean Brierley Award for Excellence in Teaching, COLA Since joining the Department of English in 1990, Professor Douglas Lanier has earned the highest praise from students for the outstanding quality of his teaching. Time-and-again students claim he is the best professor they have ever had. His energy is “intoxicating,” as one student puts it. Professor Lanier’s ability to explain complex points brings many students back to his courses again and again. Professor Lanier also has directed numerous doctoral dissertations. Many of his doctoral students have gone on to enjoy successful careers as professors and administrators at prestigious colleges and universities across the U.S. The highest appreciation for Professor Lanier’s teaching excellence extends well beyond UNH. In 2016-2017, he was appointed Fulbright Global Shakespeare Centre Distinguished Chair at Queen Mary College, University of London and the University of Warwick. Professor Lanier also served as visiting professor at the University of Milan, the Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia, and the University of Szeged in Hungary. It is impossible to do justice to the breadth and depth of Professor Douglas Lanier’s excellence in teaching in this brief statement. Even so, it is abundantly clear that Professor Lanier richly deserves the honor of receiving this year’s Jean C. Brierley Award for Excellence in College Teaching. Lisa Ranfos, 2026 Excellence in Clinical Engagement Award, CHHS Lisa Ranfos exemplifies excellence in clinical engagement through the leadership she brought to the UNH Child Study and Development Center, where teaching, mentorship, research, and service come together in remarkable ways. Under her leadership, each year hundreds of UNH students gained meaningful, hands-on experience that prepared them to become thoughtful and skilled educators. Her impact extends well beyond the university through statewide leadership, national service, and partnerships that advance the field of early childhood education. During a particularly challenging year for the CSDC community, Lisa led with steadiness, compassion, creativity, and an unwavering commitment to children, families, students, and colleagues. Her work reflects the very best of UNH’s land-grant mission: connecting academic excellence with service to our communities. It is a pleasure to recognize Lisa Ranfos with the University of New Hampshire Award for Excellence in Clinical Engagement. Michael Simmons, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, COLSA What students seem to recognize, often from the very first class, is that time with Michael is time wellspent – that something meaningful is happening. He doesn't just teach ecology — he awakens a curiosity that outlasts the course and shapes the way they see the natural world. Michael exemplifies the very best of applied, experiential teaching. Through field-intensive courses and a genuine commitment to building relationships — both with his students and between his students and the natural world — Michael has become one of the most beloved and impactful educators in the college. Students gravitate to him as an approachable teacher who makes complex ecological theory accessible, concrete, and relevant. They don't just take Michael’s courses; they become part of a learning community grounded in shared curiosity and a genuine connection to the land they study together. Colleagues feel it too. They have a deep appreciation for how Michael’s forestry expertise, collaborative spirit, and genuine kindness have strengthened our programs and enriched our community. Jeanie Sowers, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, COLA A professor in the department of Political Science and International Affairs, Jeanie Sowers teaches courses on important topics in the study of comparative politics, environmental politics, and international affairs. Her enriching courses – such as “Comparative Politics of the Middle East” or “Politics and Policy in a Warming World” attract strong enrollments and high praise from students. Sowers’s teaching and scholarly commitments are anchored by a strong interdisciplinary coherence, and whether in dynamic classroom projects or mentoring URC, IROP, INCO and McNair students, she deftly infuses this ethos. Across her classes, she brings historical, political, and economic context, and provides an invaluable humanistic perspective. Many of her student evaluations note that she brings in “the personal experiences of individuals and groups of people” who are affected by political processes. Accordingly, not only does she provide a rigorous knowledge base to her students, but also diverse perspectives and cognitive empathy. Jen Spindel, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, COLA A renowned scholar in international security, Professor Spindel is an associate professor in the department of Political Science and International Affairs. The interesting courses she teaches include such topics as weapons technology, arms transfer, civil-military relations, and military tactics. She is roundly praised for her expertise and passion, her innovative classroom and course assignments (including wargame and on-campus land war simulations), and her focus on active student learning and student peer collaboration. As a teacher and as an advisor, she is praised for her availability and approachability, and she is a much sought-out research mentor by both undergraduate and MA students. Beyond these activities, her dynamic stewardship of the New Hampshire International Seminar series places students and colleagues alike in thoughtful conversations with leading security scholars, policymakers, and other experts while also exposing our students to the range of impactful careers for which their undergraduate learning prepares them. Sean Tavares, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, College of Professional Studies Sean Tavares teaches at UNH Manchester in the mechanical engineering technology program. When Sseveral courses were in dire need of change and updates, Sean recreated and developed several new courses from scratch. The thermal science courses, Fluid Technology and Heat Transfer I and II, are prime examples. Sean developed new lecture material and designed new lab experiments. In the Control Systems and Components course, Sean developed new experiments to emphasize lecture material. Sean uses his knowledge, industry expertise, and talents to bring real world practical lab experiences to his students. He can effectively relate course material taught in the lecture and lab for student understanding. He continually adapts and makes changes so that students can understand concepts, processes, and theories. Sean is innovative in the classroom and lab environment to meet students’ needs. Sean’s students are well prepared for industry positions. Jill Trumbell, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, CHHS Jill Trumbell teaches in numerous modalities and contexts, achieving consistently exceptional student outcomes over the course of nearly 10 years at the University of New Hampshire. Her impact across the Human Development and Family Studies curriculum has uplifted her colleagues and students alike, several of whom have noted her supportive approach and commitment to innovation and student-centeredness. Reflective, inclusive, and dedicated to the art of teaching, Trumbull has succeeded in cultivating a sense of community at CHHS which extends far beyond the classroom. Her students carry with them the wisdom they have gained through Trumbull’s redesign of the Families, Schools, and Community capstone, which integrates diversity, equity, and inclusion content across coursework. Through her deeply thought-out approach, and through the work her students carry with them as they work in communities nationwide, Trumbull has impacted the complex sociocultural context in which children and families live. Paul Tsang, 2026 Distinguished Professor Award, COLSA Paul Tsang is recognized for an extraordinary 37-year record of excellence in teaching, mentorship, service, and scholarship at the University of New Hampshire. Since joining UNH in 1989, Tsang has inspired generations of students through innovative teaching, dedicated mentorship, and a genuine passion for scientific discovery. He has mentored countless undergraduate and graduate students, helping launch careers in many fields related to science and medicine. As Director of the Hamel Center for Undergraduate Research for 13 years, Tsang expanded research opportunities for students and helped establish the Undergraduate Research Conference as a major university tradition. The URC represents a remarkable contribution to the university’s culture of discovery. Alongside this leadership, Tsang has maintained an impressive record of funded research, publications, and professional service. Through his extraordinary generosity, leadership, and lifelong commitment to students and UNH, Tsang has made a lasting and profound impact on the university community. Heather Ward, 2026 Excellence in Teaching Award, UNH Franklin Pierce School of Law For the past six years, Heather Ward has taught legal research, analysis, and writing, criminal law, and other courses to residential and hybrid students at UNH Franklin Pierce School of Law.  Her high standards and student-centered approach are the hallmark of her teaching career. In the words of one of her students, “Professor Ward possesses a unique ability to balance incredibly high expectations with recognition of the individual student’s way of learning.”  This combination of rigor and supportive guidance has shaped the legal minds of many of the state’s newest attorneys. Professor Ward is an alumna of UNH Franklin Pierce and, before becoming a professor, had a distinguished career as a law clerk, in civil practice, and as a public defender. Her fierce intellect and steadfast commitment to fostering an educational environment where everyone can thrive make her a pillar of the law school community, the bar, and the state. title: UNH Launches Ocean Innovation Startup Residency Program - University of New Hampshire
content: UNH has launched the Ocean Innovation Startup Residency program, a founder-centered, in-person program designed for early-stage startups working at the intersection of technology and the ocean. Over nine months, resident companies gain access to UNH's marine science expertise, select testing facilities, industry network, and hands-on mentorship — all at no cost and with no equity taken. The first program of its kind in New Hampshire, the Ocean Innovation Startup Residency leverages UNH’s world-class marine assets, Sea Grant status, longstanding partnerships with NOAA, and regional industry network to support early-stage ocean and marine technology startups. Application deadline for the nine-month residency is Jan. 15, 2027; the residency runs from April 1, 2027 - December 17, 2027. Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. All rights reserved.

title: Rick Atkinson speaks at UNH's Rutman Distinguished Lecture Series - The New Hampshire
content: On Tuesday, Oct. 20, the University of New Hampshire welcomed Pulitzer-prize winning journalist and historian, Rick Atkinson to speak for this year's Rutman Lecture Series in the Memorial Union Building (MUB). The Rutman Lecture Series began in 2013 and has since invited academics to speak on American Presidencies, Atkinson chose to analyze the first and most famous president, George Washington. Specifically, Atkinson looked at Washington through the lens of war using his knowledge from writing eight narrative history books about five wars including the American Revolution. “Where does a writer begin writing about George Washington?” Said Atkinson. Atkinson and other historians have the unique challenge of describing events with details that are found purely through research. Atkinson found many characteristics of Washington that are commonly overlooked, describing him as opaque, molten tempered and pitiful of himself. Washington was not the best general either, and when he was promoted to commander in chief, he read what Atkinson described as a “war for dummies” handbook due to his lack of experience. A question Atkinson explored in his lecture was, If Washington was not fit for the role of commander in chief and had unpleasant characteristics, why has he been put on such a pedestal by Americans? Atkinson explained that Washington had a higher calling as a leader. “Washington has the ability to rise to the occasion,” said Atkinson. Washington had instincts to know the most optimal way to influence and compromise as a leader. On another note, Atkinson described Washington as physically robust considering he never caught a cold during the war. It also helped that Washington was six-foot-two in a time when the average height of a man was five feet eight inches, giving him further physical advantages. Washington’s character was not the only thing overlooked by many Americans, the Revolutionary War itself was relentlessly violent on all sides of combat, as Atkinson described. The American side had many flaws itself. The rebel government in Pennsylvania would execute anyone suspected of being a traitor or loyal to the British. Atkinson highlighted that the Americans were truly relentless in their battle, even when faced with many cities burning and falling. “Even a profounding British triumph would not have been enough”, said Atkinson. Atkinson has written about war time and time again because it “shapes our history.” It has been prevalent in our history nationally and globally. Atkinson informed the audience that only 268 years have been without war out of over three thousand years of recorded human history. “Unfortunately none of those 268 years have any of us been alive,” said Atkinson. title: Leaner and Meaner: Are UNH's Profits Getting Bigger? Buy Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH is becoming more profitable while serving fewer members. Third-quarter results suggest that Optum's turnaround efforts and UnitedHealthcare's pricing discipline are restoring margins, even as revenues and enrollment face pressure. However, sustaining this recovery will require continued execution, tight medical-cost management and an ability to navigate a changing political landscape. Is UNH positioned for lasting earnings growth? Optum leads that shift. Its operating earnings increased to $3.73 billion from $2.51 billion, as revenues declined to $66.9 billion from $69.2 billion. At Optum Health, operating profit rose to $735 million from just $41 million. Its margin reached 3.2% compared with a 0.2% margin a year earlier. Discipline is returning, although margin remains well below management's target of 6-8% by 2028. Optum Health's revenues declined 10% to $22.9 billion as the company withdrew from markets where its value-based care presence lacked sufficient scale. While the retreat helps eliminate underperforming arrangements, sustained profitability will depend on expanding patient relationships within established markets. Optum Health currently serves about 20 million patients, including roughly 4 million in fully accountable care arrangements, leaving room to deepen its integrated care model. Growth opportunities include home health, surgery centers and complex-care management, where earlier intervention could reduce costly hospitalizations. Home health visits increased 10% in the quarter, while online self-scheduling rose 27%, indicating progress in patient access. The challenge now is converting these operational improvements into sustainable revenue growth and higher margins. Two other Optum businesses provide an earnings cushion. Optum Insight's operating earnings reached $1.28 billion, up from $920 million, on revenue growth of about 3%. Operating margin jumped to 23.4% from 17.3% a year ago. Automation could lower claims-processing and documentation costs for customers. A new coding product has 15 live clients, with 24 more being implemented. Optum Rx is also finding ways to earn more from less volume. Operating earnings climbed to $1.72 billion from $1.55 billion, although adjusted prescriptions fell to 393 million from 414 million. Greater biosimilar adoption and operational improvements supported profitability. Specialty pharmacy volumes, meanwhile, increased 2.6%, even as overall scripts declined. More than half of Optum Rx membership now comes from outside UnitedHealthcare, reducing its reliance on its sister insurer. Transparent, fee-based pricing could strengthen customer retention as pharmacy benefit managers face demands for simpler drug economics. Its operating margin of 4.3% grew 40 bps from a year ago. UnitedHealthcare's numbers tell a similar story. Its operating earnings rose to $2.83 billion from $1.81 billion, despite revenues easing to $86.3 billion from $87.1 billion. The operating margin improved to 3.3% from 2.1%. At the group level, the medical care ratio dropped to 88.4% from 89.9%, while the operating cost ratio fell to 12.8% from 13.5%. Better pricing, benefit design and claims management are helping the insurer keep more of each premium dollar. However, the medical care ratio benefited from $610 million of favorable reserve development related to earlier 2026 service periods. UnitedHealthcare enters 2027 with a narrower, potentially healthier book of business. Medical membership fell to 48.3 million from 50.1 million a year ago, reflecting deliberate Medicare Advantage repositioning and other losses. Growth is shifting toward special needs plans. UNH is concentrating on high-value HMOs and plans serving people with chronic conditions or dual eligibility, where coordinated care can support both outcomes and economics. The Democrats' victory in the midterm elections could reshape the healthcare industry's policy outlook. Set to control both chambers of Congress from January 2027, Democrats may push to reverse Medicaid funding cuts and restore subsidies. Such measures could support insurance enrollment and ease funding pressures on healthcare providers. However, the benefits may vary across insurers. Medicaid-focused players like Molina Healthcare, Inc. MOH and Centene Corporation CNC could gain more directly than UnitedHealth, given UNH's substantial Medicare Advantage exposure. Meanwhile, increased congressional oversight of Medicare Advantage practices, prior authorizations and pharmacy benefit managers could create fresh challenges for UnitedHealthcare and Optum Rx. President Trump's veto power and legislative hurdles could delay major policy changes. For UNH, the election introduces potential funding relief but also regulatory uncertainty, making execution and policy developments important determinants of its recovery. Looking at the year-to-date period, UNH stock has gained 19.4%, outperforming the S&P 500’s 7.2% rise, but trailing the industry’s 22.9% growth. Peers like Molina Healthcareand Centenehave increased 20.5% and 69.5%, respectively, during this time. Commercial medical-cost trends continue to exceed UNH's expectations, driven partly by costly specialty drugs and payment disputes under the No Surprises Act. Although pricing adjustments and operational improvements are supporting margins, shrinking insurance membership and lower Optum Health revenues leave less room for execution errors. Medicaid reimbursement rates have also struggled to keep pace with patient acuity, with management expecting core Medicaid margins to remain moderately better than negative 1% in 2026. Persistent funding mismatches could delay profitability improvements, particularly if medical utilization remains elevated. Profit growth appears achievable if medical-cost pressures remain manageable. Management raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $20.50 and considers the lower end of its long-term 13-16% growth target a reasonable starting point for 2027. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS stands at $20.61, indicating 26.1% year-over-year growth, while revenues are projected at $449.11 billion, up 0.4%. For 2027, EPS is expected to rise 13.4% to $23.38, alongside 3.2% revenue growth to $463.41 billion. Estimate revisions reinforce the positive outlook, with 14 upward EPS revisions for 2026 and 13 for 2027 over the past month, against no cuts. The company beat earnings estimates in each of the past four quarters, producing an average earnings surprise of 14%. In comparison, Molina and Centene are currently priced at 23.01X and 12.73X, respectively, both higher than their own five-year median multiples. Wall Street also sees room for further gains for UNH. Despite the stock’s ytd rise, the average analyst price target of $475.96 suggests an upside of 20.3% from current levels. Individual targets range from $380 to $531, indicating that analysts remain divided over the pace and extent of UnitedHealth's recovery. UnitedHealth's recovery is gaining traction, with improved insurance margins, Optum's operational turnaround and greater cost discipline supporting profitability despite a smaller membership base. The company's focus on higher-value care arrangements and profitable growth provides a foundation for sustained earnings improvement, although elevated medical costs and reimbursement pressures remain challenges. Encouraging earnings estimate revisions, management's constructive 2027 outlook and a valuation below historical levels strengthen the investment case. While healthcare policy uncertainty warrants monitoring, UNH's improving fundamentals and earnings growth potential support its Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).
